name: Blessing
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Blessing: a weapon edge glowing white-hot. A priest touches a spear-point and names a god.
details: Battle · 4 mana · target ally stack · Ally rolls its maximum damage through the current and next round.
lore: A priest touches a spear-point and names a god. For a little while every blow lands as if aimed by that god’s own hand.

name: Far Sight
shown_on: Spellbook; Adventure map cast buttons; Encyclopedia
brief: Far Sight: an eye opening over a map. Shepherds’ magic: look at a hill long enough and you can see what grazes on its far side.
details: Adventure · 5 mana · target known tile · Adventure only: reveal radius 2 around a known tile until next dawn. · expanded content
lore: Shepherds’ magic: look at a hill long enough and you can see what grazes on its far side.

name: Hearthlight
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Hearthlight: a warm light closing a wound. A glow like the fire of home, carried into the field.
details: Battle · 4 mana · target ally stack · Heal up to 12 + 4 × Power of the front creature’s missing HP; no resurrection. · expanded content
lore: A glow like the fire of home, carried into the field. Wounds close a little, as they do when a mother is near.

name: Ill Omen
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Ill Omen: a thread being cut short, a weapon dulled. Every army has a soldier who sees a crow on the left and loses heart.
details: Battle · 5 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy stack rolls its minimum damage through the current and next round (a Blessing on it cancels out). · expanded content
lore: Every army has a soldier who sees a crow on the left and loses heart. The spell finds that soldier in every rank at once and makes him right.

name: Shield of Faith
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Shield of Faith: a shield wall turning a blade. Priests of every road-shrine teach the same prayer: not for victory, only that the next blow land a little lighter.
details: Battle · 5 mana · target ally stack · Ally takes ×0.8 damage from melee strikes through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: Priests of every road-shrine teach the same prayer: not for victory, only that the next blow land a little lighter. Soldiers say it under their breath before the lines meet.

name: Spark
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Spark: a bolt or burst striking one target. The first thing every apprentice learns: a crack of light between two fingers, thrown hard.
details: Battle · 4 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy stack takes 10 + 5 × Power direct damage.
lore: The first thing every apprentice learns: a crack of light between two fingers, thrown hard. Masters never stop using it.

name: Swiftness
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Swiftness: winged light at a runner’s heels. Spoken over a soldier’s feet, it makes the ground feel like a downhill road.
details: Battle · 4 mana · target ally stack · Ally +2 Speed through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: Spoken over a soldier’s feet, it makes the ground feel like a downhill road.

name: War Cry
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: War Cry: a weapon wreathed in a golden aura. A shout that is half prayer, half threat.
details: Battle · 4 mana · target ally stack · Ally +3 Attack through the current and next round.
lore: A shout that is half prayer, half threat. Soldiers who hear it remember why they came.

name: Ward
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Ward: a shield of light in front of a warrior. A circle drawn in the air around a company.
details: Battle · 4 mana · target ally stack · Ally +3 Defense through the current and next round.
lore: A circle drawn in the air around a company. Patron gods grant it to those who keep their oaths.

name: Clear Skies
shown_on: Spellbook; Adventure map cast buttons; Encyclopedia
brief: Clear Skies: an eye opening over a map. Sailors pay well for it: one day without fog, and a whole valley laid out like a map.
details: Adventure · 8 mana · target known tile · Adventure only: reveal radius 4 around a known tile until next dawn. · expanded content
lore: Sailors pay well for it: one day without fog, and a whole valley laid out like a map.

name: Ember Burst
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Ember Burst: an explosion spreading over a small area. A handful of coals from the forge, thrown with a word.
details: Battle · 8 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy stack and every enemy stack beside it take 12 + 5 × Power damage. · expanded content
lore: A handful of coals from the forge, thrown with a word. Smiths invented it to keep thieves from their yards; captains made it a weapon.

name: Fleet Foot
shown_on: Spellbook; Adventure map cast buttons; Encyclopedia
brief: Fleet Foot: a road unrolling under winged feet. Couriers’ magic: the day stretches a little longer for whoever carries urgent news.
details: Adventure · 6 mana · target self · Adventure only: the caster gains 200 movement points today. · expanded content
lore: Couriers’ magic: the day stretches a little longer for whoever carries urgent news.

name: Lightning
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Lightning: a bolt or burst striking one target. The sky-father’s weapon, borrowed for one stroke.
details: Battle · 6 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy stack takes 25 + 10 × Power direct damage.
lore: The sky-father’s weapon, borrowed for one stroke. Those who ask too often find the sky stops answering.

name: Mend
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Mend: a warm light closing a wound. Field-surgeons’ magic, plain and practical: flesh remembers being whole and is persuaded to be so again.
details: Battle · 5 mana · target ally stack · Heal up to 20 + 5 × Power of the front creature’s missing HP; no resurrection.
lore: Field-surgeons’ magic, plain and practical: flesh remembers being whole and is persuaded to be so again.

name: Sapping Touch
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Sapping Touch: a weapon wreathed in a golden aura. The fever-healer’s art turned backwards: instead of drawing sickness out, it pours weariness in.
details: Battle · 6 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy −3 Attack through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: The fever-healer’s art turned backwards: instead of drawing sickness out, it pours weariness in.

name: Steadfast
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Steadfast: a shield of light in front of a warrior. Old sergeants call it the stubborn spell.
details: Battle · 6 mana · target ally stack · Ally +4 Defense through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: Old sergeants call it the stubborn spell. It does not make soldiers braver, only harder to move.

name: Veil
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Veil: arrows deflected by a dome of light. A shimmer in the air like heat over stones.
details: Battle · 6 mana · target ally stack · Ally takes ×0.75 damage from ranged strikes through the current and next round.
lore: A shimmer in the air like heat over stones. Arrows lose their way in it.

name: Weariness
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Weariness: winged light at a runner’s heels. Every soldier knows the hour before dawn when the shield gets heavy.
details: Battle · 5 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy −2 Speed through the current and next round (never below 1). · expanded content
lore: Every soldier knows the hour before dawn when the shield gets heavy. This spell brings that hour early.

name: Divine Sight
shown_on: Spellbook; Adventure map cast buttons; Encyclopedia
brief: Divine Sight: an eye opening over a map. Gods see the whole world at once.
details: Adventure · 10 mana · target known tile · Adventure only: reveal radius 3 around a known tile until next dawn.
lore: Gods see the whole world at once. For a single night, they lend a hero a corner of that view.

name: Homecoming
shown_on: Spellbook; Adventure map cast buttons; Encyclopedia
brief: Homecoming: a portal back to a town gate. Every hearth remembers the one who left it.
details: Adventure · 14 mana · target self · Adventure only: the caster returns to the nearest town you own; its movement ends for the day. · expanded content
lore: Every hearth remembers the one who left it. The spell lets that memory pull the hero home.

name: Leaden Air
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Leaden Air: a banner of light over a whole army. The air over the enemy turns thick as summer before a storm.
details: Battle · 11 mana · target enemy army · Every enemy stack −1 Speed through the current and next round (never below 1). · expanded content
lore: The air over the enemy turns thick as summer before a storm. Horses balk; even birds fly low.

name: Rallying Hymn
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Rallying Hymn: a banner of light over a whole army. Every people has a song it sings when the line is about to break.
details: Battle · 10 mana · target friendly army · Every friendly stack +3 Defense through the current round. · expanded content
lore: Every people has a song it sings when the line is about to break. The spell lets the whole army hear it at once.

name: Renewal
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Renewal: healing light falling like rain over an army. Springtime, called down for a moment over a battlefield.
details: Battle · 12 mana · target friendly army · The front creature of every friendly stack heals up to 10 + 5 × Power HP (no resurrection). · expanded content
lore: Springtime, called down for a moment over a battlefield. It cannot bring back the dead, but it remembers the living.

name: Starfall
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Starfall: fire or stars falling over an enemy army. On the night the old gods quarrelled, stars fell on both their armies.
details: Battle · 14 mana · target enemy army · Every enemy stack takes 10 + 4 × Power damage. · expanded content
lore: On the night the old gods quarrelled, stars fell on both their armies. Astronomers learned to ask for a few more — but only over the enemy.

name: Bramble Snare
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Bramble Snare: winged light at a runner’s heels. Hawthorn is the fairies’ tree; cut it and it takes revenge.
details: Battle · 4 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy −2 Speed through the current round (never below 1). · expanded content
lore: Hawthorn is the fairies’ tree; cut it and it takes revenge. The druids simply ask it to reach for the enemy’s ankles.

name: Cauldron of the Dagda
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Cauldron of the Dagda: a warm light closing a wound. No one ever left the Dagda’s cauldron hungry.
details: Battle · 7 mana · target ally stack · Heal up to 25 + 6 × Power of the front creature’s missing HP; no resurrection. · expanded content
lore: No one ever left the Dagda’s cauldron hungry. A ladle of its broth, summoned to the field, mends what hunger and steel have opened.

name: Glamour
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Glamour: a weapon wreathed in a golden aura. The Fair Folk’s favourite trick: make a sword look like a stick, a captain like a fool.
details: Battle · 6 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy −3 Attack through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: The Fair Folk’s favourite trick: make a sword look like a stick, a captain like a fool. The enemy forgets how to fight.

name: Mist of Manannán
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Mist of Manannán: a banner of light over a whole army. The sea god hides his islands behind a cloak of mist.
details: Battle · 11 mana · target enemy army · Every enemy stack −2 Speed through the current and next round (never below 1). · expanded content
lore: The sea god hides his islands behind a cloak of mist. Druids borrow a corner of it, and the enemy marches in circles.

name: Wild Hunt
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Wild Hunt: an explosion spreading over a small area. Hounds, horns and riders out of the storm.
details: Battle · 13 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy stack and every enemy stack beside it take 25 + 9 × Power damage. · expanded content
lore: Hounds, horns and riders out of the storm. Whatever the Hunt passes over is never quite the same.

name: Ankh of Renewal
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Ankh of Renewal: a warm light closing a wound. The key of life, held to a wound.
details: Battle · 4 mana · target ally stack · Heal up to 15 + 5 × Power of the front creature’s missing HP; no resurrection. · expanded content
lore: The key of life, held to a wound. Temple healers say the ankh does not heal — it only reminds the body what it was.

name: Eye of Horus
shown_on: Spellbook; Adventure map cast buttons; Encyclopedia
brief: Eye of Horus: an eye opening over a map. The falcon god lost an eye fighting for his father’s throne; it was healed and became a charm of seeing.
details: Adventure · 8 mana · target known tile · Adventure only: reveal radius 5 around a known tile until next dawn. · expanded content
lore: The falcon god lost an eye fighting for his father’s throne; it was healed and became a charm of seeing.

name: Wrath of Sekhmet
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Wrath of Sekhmet: a bolt or burst striking one target. The lioness once nearly devoured mankind and was calmed only with red beer.
details: Battle · 8 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy stack takes 22 + 9 × Power direct damage. · expanded content
lore: The lioness once nearly devoured mankind and was calmed only with red beer. Her priests can still wake a little of that rage — and point it.

name: Balance of Ma’at
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Balance of Ma’at: healing light falling like rain over an army. On the scale of judgement a heart is weighed against a feather.
details: Battle · 13 mana · target friendly army · The front creature of every friendly stack heals up to 12 + 6 × Power HP (no resurrection). · expanded content
lore: On the scale of judgement a heart is weighed against a feather. Ma’at restores what was taken unjustly — and in battle, much is.

name: Scarab Swarm
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Scarab Swarm: an explosion spreading over a small area. The scarab rolls the sun across the sky.
details: Battle · 10 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy stack and every enemy stack beside it take 15 + 6 × Power damage. · expanded content
lore: The scarab rolls the sun across the sky. When angered, a thousand of them roll over whatever stands in the way.

name: Hoplon Wall
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Hoplon Wall: a shield wall turning a blade. Each round shield covers the neighbour’s left side; the line stands or falls together.
details: Battle · 5 mana · target ally stack · Ally takes ×0.75 damage from melee strikes through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: Each round shield covers the neighbour’s left side; the line stands or falls together. The spell locks the shields edge to edge as if one smith had forged them all.

name: Apollo’s Arrow
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Apollo’s Arrow: a bolt or burst striking one target. The far-shooting god’s arrows brought plague to the proud and light to the faithful.
details: Battle · 8 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy stack takes 20 + 8 × Power direct damage. · expanded content
lore: The far-shooting god’s arrows brought plague to the proud and light to the faithful. His priests ask only for one arrow, and aim it themselves.

name: Wings of Hermes
shown_on: Spellbook; Adventure map cast buttons; Encyclopedia
brief: Wings of Hermes: a road unrolling under winged feet. The messenger of the gods never walked when he could run, and never ran when he could fly.
details: Adventure · 7 mana · target self · Adventure only: the caster gains 150 movement points today. · expanded content
lore: The messenger of the gods never walked when he could run, and never ran when he could fly. Heralds who honour him find the road shorter.

name: Aegis
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Aegis: a banner of light over a whole army. The goatskin shield of the sky-father, lent to his daughter of wisdom.
details: Battle · 9 mana · target friendly army · Every friendly stack +2 Defense through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: The goatskin shield of the sky-father, lent to his daughter of wisdom. Its shadow over an army turns aside every second blow.

name: Thunderclap
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Thunderclap: an explosion spreading over a small area. The noise of the king of the gods losing his temper.
details: Battle · 12 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy stack and every enemy stack beside it take 20 + 8 × Power damage. · expanded content
lore: The noise of the king of the gods losing his temper. Anyone close enough to hear it is close enough to be hurt.

name: Kitsune-bi
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Kitsune-bi: a bolt or burst striking one target. Fox-fire drifts over the rice paddies on autumn nights.
details: Battle · 5 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy stack takes 12 + 5 × Power direct damage. · expanded content
lore: Fox-fire drifts over the rice paddies on autumn nights. Travellers who follow it are lost; enemies who are followed by it burn.

name: Blossom Veil
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Blossom Veil: a shield of light in front of a warrior. Cherry blossoms fall for only a few days.
details: Battle · 6 mana · target ally stack · Ally +5 Defense through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: Cherry blossoms fall for only a few days. While they fall, nothing sharp seems to reach the one they cover.

name: Mirror of Yata
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Mirror of Yata: arrows deflected by a dome of light. A mirror once drew the sun goddess out of her cave.
details: Battle · 7 mana · target ally stack · Ally takes ×0.5 damage from ranged strikes through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: A mirror once drew the sun goddess out of her cave. Its reflection, cast over a company, turns arrows aside like light from polished bronze.

name: Divine Wind
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Divine Wind: a banner of light over a whole army. A wind sent by the gods once scattered an invading fleet.
details: Battle · 8 mana · target friendly army · Every friendly stack +2 Speed through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: A wind sent by the gods once scattered an invading fleet. Called over an army, it pushes every soldier forward.

name: Raijin’s Drums
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Raijin’s Drums: fire or stars falling over an enemy army. The thunder god beats a ring of drums across the sky.
details: Battle · 14 mana · target enemy army · Every enemy stack takes 12 + 5 × Power damage. · expanded content
lore: The thunder god beats a ring of drums across the sky. When his shrine-maidens dance, he sometimes beats them over the enemy’s camp.

name: Jaguar Spirit
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Jaguar Spirit: a weapon wreathed in a golden aura. The jaguar hunts by night and by surprise.
details: Battle · 5 mana · target ally stack · Ally +4 Attack through the current round. · expanded content
lore: The jaguar hunts by night and by surprise. Warriors who wear its pelt call its spirit into their arms for one leap.

name: Rain of Tlaloc
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Rain of Tlaloc: healing light falling like rain over an army. The rain god keeps four jars: one waters the maize, the others bring frost, drought and blight.
details: Battle · 8 mana · target friendly army · The front creature of every friendly stack heals up to 8 + 4 × Power HP (no resurrection). · expanded content
lore: The rain god keeps four jars: one waters the maize, the others bring frost, drought and blight. His priests pray only for the first.

name: Smoking Mirror
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Smoking Mirror: a weapon wreathed in a golden aura. Tezcatlipoca’s obsidian mirror shows each man his own death.
details: Battle · 7 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy −4 Attack through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: Tezcatlipoca’s obsidian mirror shows each man his own death. Those who glimpse it fight like men already beaten.

name: Fifth Sun
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Fifth Sun: a banner of light over a whole army. Four suns have died and the fifth is kept alive by sacrifice.
details: Battle · 12 mana · target friendly army · Every friendly stack +3 Attack through the current round. · expanded content
lore: Four suns have died and the fifth is kept alive by sacrifice. For one round, every warrior burns with its light.

name: Obsidian Rain
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Obsidian Rain: an explosion spreading over a small area. Volcanic glass falls like hail from a sky the colour of smoke.
details: Battle · 11 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy stack and every enemy stack beside it take 15 + 7 × Power damage. · expanded content
lore: Volcanic glass falls like hail from a sky the colour of smoke. Priests say the mountain is only returning what was taken from it.

name: Rune of Tyr
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Rune of Tyr: a weapon wreathed in a golden aura. Tyr gave his hand to bind the wolf.
details: Battle · 5 mana · target ally stack · Ally +4 Attack through the current round. · expanded content
lore: Tyr gave his hand to bind the wolf. Warriors cut his arrow-rune on their blades and ask him for one honest stroke.

name: Frost Breath
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Frost Breath: winged light at a runner’s heels. The breath of the frost giants, who were here before the gods.
details: Battle · 6 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy −3 Speed through the current and next round (never below 1). · expanded content
lore: The breath of the frost giants, who were here before the gods. Joints stiffen, feet freeze to the ground.

name: The Norns’ Thread
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: The Norns’ Thread: a thread being cut short, a weapon dulled. At the root of the world-tree three women spin every life.
details: Battle · 7 mana · target enemy stack · Enemy stack rolls its minimum damage through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: At the root of the world-tree three women spin every life. A völva who knows the right song can make them shorten one thread — for a little while.

name: Berserkergang
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Berserkergang: a banner of light over a whole army. Bear-shirted warriors who bite their shields and feel no wounds.
details: Battle · 9 mana · target friendly army · Every friendly stack +2 Attack through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: Bear-shirted warriors who bite their shields and feel no wounds. The spell spreads their madness through the ranks — briefly.

name: Gjallarhorn
shown_on: Spellbook; Battle spell choice (when several can be cast); Encyclopedia
brief: Gjallarhorn: a banner of light over a whole army. Heimdall will blow the horn once, at the end of all things.
details: Battle · 12 mana · target enemy army · Every enemy stack −2 Attack through the current and next round. · expanded content
lore: Heimdall will blow the horn once, at the end of all things. Its echo, called up by a skald, is enough to make an enemy feel that the end has come.

name: Lacquered Ō-yoroi
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Lacquered Ō-yoroi — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Hundreds of lacquered scales laced with silk in the colours of a house.
details: major · +2 commander Defense and +1 morale. · set: Treasures of Takamagahara · expanded content
lore: Hundreds of lacquered scales laced with silk in the colours of a house. Soldiers recognise the colours across a field and stand firmer.

name: Linen Cuirass
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Linen Cuirass — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Layers of linen glued and stitched until they are as stiff as wood.
details: minor · +1 commander Defense.
lore: Layers of linen glued and stitched until they are as stiff as wood. Cheaper than bronze and cooler in summer.

name: Mail of the Einherjar
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Mail of the Einherjar — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. The chosen dead fight every day in the hall of the slain and are whole again by evening.
details: major · +3 commander Defense. · set: Arms of the Einherjar · expanded content
lore: The chosen dead fight every day in the hall of the slain and are whole again by evening. Their mail mends with them.

name: Quilted Cotton Armor
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Quilted Cotton Armor — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Two fingers of salt-hardened cotton, stitched tight.
details: minor · +2 commander Defense. · expanded content
lore: Two fingers of salt-hardened cotton, stitched tight. Conquerors from over the sea laughed at it, then traded their steel for it.

name: Scale Hauberk
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Scale Hauberk — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Overlapping bronze scales on a leather shirt, like the skin of a river serpent.
details: minor · +2 commander Defense.
lore: Overlapping bronze scales on a leather shirt, like the skin of a river serpent.

name: Scarab-scale Corselet
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Scarab-scale Corselet — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Bronze scales shaped like beetles that roll the sun across the sky.
details: major · +2 commander Defense and +1 mana at dawn. · set: Regalia of the Two Lands · expanded content
lore: Bronze scales shaped like beetles that roll the sun across the sky. The corselet is warm at dawn, as if it knows.

name: Jaguar-pelt Cape
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Jaguar-pelt Cape — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Only a warrior who has taken four captives may wear the jaguar.
details: major · Tier 1–3 creatures +1 Attack in battle. · expanded content
lore: Only a warrior who has taken four captives may wear the jaguar. Young soldiers fight harder near one, hoping to earn their own.

name: Nemean Lionskin
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Nemean Lionskin — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. No blade could cut the lion of Nemea; the hero strangled it and flayed it with its own claws.
details: relic · +3 commander Defense. Unique. · expanded content
lore: No blade could cut the lion of Nemea; the hero strangled it and flayed it with its own claws. The pelt still turns steel.

name: Raven-feather Cloak
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Raven-feather Cloak — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. The battle-crow goddess flies over every field before the fighting.
details: minor · +10% daily land movement. · expanded content
lore: The battle-crow goddess flies over every field before the fighting. A cloak of her feathers makes the road feel like flight.

name: Wanderer’s Grey Cloak
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Wanderer’s Grey Cloak — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A broad-brimmed traveller in a grey cloak asks for a seat by every fire and listens more than he speaks.
details: major · +2 hexes of vision and +5% daily land movement. · expanded content
lore: A broad-brimmed traveller in a grey cloak asks for a seat by every fire and listens more than he speaks. Some say he leaves his cloak behind for those who listen too.

name: Wayfarer’s Cloak
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Wayfarer’s Cloak — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A heavy travelling cloak with deep pockets and a hood that keeps out rain from any direction.
details: minor · +1 commander Defense and +1 hex of vision. Wayfarer’s Kit. · set: Wayfarer’s Kit · expanded content
lore: A heavy travelling cloak with deep pockets and a hood that keeps out rain from any direction.

name: Boots of the Long Road
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Boots of the Long Road — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Cobbled for a pilgrim who swore to visit every shrine of every god.
details: major · +15% daily land movement. · expanded content
lore: Cobbled for a pilgrim who swore to visit every shrine of every god. He made it, they say, and the boots outlived him.

name: Scribe’s Papyrus Sandals
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Scribe’s Papyrus Sandals — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Woven reed sandals of the temple scribes, who walked between the granaries counting everything.
details: treasure · +1 commander Knowledge and +5% daily land movement. · expanded content
lore: Woven reed sandals of the temple scribes, who walked between the granaries counting everything. Light, quiet and quick.

name: Skis of Ullr
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Skis of Ullr — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. The god of the hunt crosses the winter faster on his skis than a horse on summer roads.
details: major · +15% daily land movement. · expanded content
lore: The god of the hunt crosses the winter faster on his skis than a horse on summer roads. He lends them to anyone who swears by his ring.

name: Tengu Geta
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Tengu Geta — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Tall one-toothed sandals of the mountain goblins, who taught swordsmanship to a boy in the forest.
details: minor · +10% daily land movement and +1 hex of vision. · expanded content
lore: Tall one-toothed sandals of the mountain goblins, who taught swordsmanship to a boy in the forest. Wearers walk the ridges as if on a road.

name: Wayfarer’s Boots
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Wayfarer’s Boots — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Boots resoled so many times that nothing of the first pair remains — except, perhaps, the luck.
details: minor · +10% daily land movement. Wayfarer’s Kit. · set: Wayfarer’s Kit · expanded content
lore: Boots resoled so many times that nothing of the first pair remains — except, perhaps, the luck.

name: Winged Sandals
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Winged Sandals — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Sandals with small wings at the heel, of the kind the messenger god wears.
details: minor · +10% daily land movement.
lore: Sandals with small wings at the heel, of the kind the messenger god wears. These are a mortal smith’s copy, and almost as good.

name: Boar-crested Helm
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Boar-crested Helm — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A bronze boar rides the crest, bristles raised.
details: minor · +2 commander Defense. · expanded content
lore: A bronze boar rides the crest, bristles raised. Northern smiths believed the boar watched over a sleeping warrior and woke him before an ambush.

name: Cap of Darkness
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Cap of Darkness — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Made by the Cyclopes for the lord of the dead, it hides its wearer from every eye.
details: major · +2 hexes of adventure vision and +1 Luck. · set: Gear of Perseus · expanded content
lore: Made by the Cyclopes for the lord of the dead, it hides its wearer from every eye. A hero who wears it sees much and is seldom seen.

name: Crested Helm
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Crested Helm — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A bronze helm with a horsehair crest that makes a man look a head taller in the front rank.
details: minor · +1 commander Defense. Panoply of the Phalanx. · set: Panoply of the Phalanx · expanded content
lore: A bronze helm with a horsehair crest that makes a man look a head taller in the front rank.

name: Crown of Counsel
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Crown of Counsel — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A crown given to a queen who never made a decision without hearing the poorest of her people first.
details: minor · +1 commander Spell Power and +1 Knowledge.
lore: A crown given to a queen who never made a decision without hearing the poorest of her people first.

name: Dragon Kabuto
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Dragon Kabuto — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A lacquered helmet with a gilded dragon between its horns.
details: minor · +1 commander Attack and +1 Defense. · set: Treasures of Takamagahara · expanded content
lore: A lacquered helmet with a gilded dragon between its horns. It was made for a general who never once turned his back on a battle.

name: Mistletoe Crown
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Mistletoe Crown — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Cut from an oak with a golden sickle on the sixth night of the moon.
details: minor · +2 commander Knowledge. · expanded content
lore: Cut from an oak with a golden sickle on the sixth night of the moon. Druids wear it when they must remember everything at once.

name: Nemes of Ra
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Nemes of Ra — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. The striped headcloth of kings, gold and lapis for the sun and the night sky.
details: major · +1 commander Spell Power and +1 Knowledge. · set: Regalia of the Two Lands · expanded content
lore: The striped headcloth of kings, gold and lapis for the sun and the night sky. Whoever wears it speaks with the authority of both.

name: Quetzal War Crown
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Quetzal War Crown — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Green plumes of the sacred bird, worth more than gold.
details: major · +1 commander Attack and +1 morale. · set: Gifts of the Feathered Serpent · expanded content
lore: Green plumes of the sacred bird, worth more than gold. A captain who wears them is seen from across the battlefield — that is the point.

name: Seer’s Circlet
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Seer’s Circlet — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A thin silver band worn by oracles, who see further with their eyes closed.
details: minor · +1 commander Spell Power.
lore: A thin silver band worn by oracles, who see further with their eyes closed.

name: Sun Diadem
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Sun Diadem — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A diadem of gold rays, worn by a priest-king who was the sun’s representative on earth.
details: minor · +2 commander Spell Power. Regalia of the Sun King. · set: Regalia of the Sun King · expanded content
lore: A diadem of gold rays, worn by a priest-king who was the sun’s representative on earth.

name: Bronze Standard
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Bronze Standard — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A bronze eagle on an ash pole.
details: minor · +1 morale for the army.
lore: A bronze eagle on an ash pole. Where it stands, the line stands.

name: Cauldron of Plenty
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Cauldron of Plenty — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. The second treasure of the gods of Ireland.
details: relic · After a won battle each stack regains 10% of its losses; +1 morale. Unique. · set: Treasures of the Tuatha Dé · expanded content
lore: The second treasure of the gods of Ireland. It fed every company that came to it, and none went away unsatisfied.

name: Champion’s Banner
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Champion’s Banner — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A tattered banner whose emblem has faded.
details: minor · +1 morale for the army. Relics of the Fallen Champion. · set: Relics of the Fallen Champion · expanded content
lore: A tattered banner whose emblem has faded. Soldiers still know what it means.

name: Cornucopia
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Cornucopia — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. The horn of the goat who nursed the king of the gods, broken off and filled forever.
details: relic · +200 Gold, +1 Wood and +1 Stone per day. Unique. · expanded content
lore: The horn of the goat who nursed the king of the gods, broken off and filled forever. Armies that carry it never forage.

name: Djed Amulet
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Djed Amulet — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. The backbone of the god who died and rose again.
details: major · After a won battle each stack regains 10% of its losses (floored). · expanded content
lore: The backbone of the god who died and rose again. Soldiers carry it so that what falls may stand up.

name: Kibisis
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Kibisis — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. The silver satchel that carried the monster’s head.
details: minor · +10% battle experience. · set: Gear of Perseus · expanded content
lore: The silver satchel that carried the monster’s head. Whatever goes into it — trophies, stories, lessons — comes out larger.

name: Knucklebone Charm
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Knucklebone Charm — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Five sheep knucklebones from a game soldiers play in camp.
details: minor · +1 Luck for the army.
lore: Five sheep knucklebones from a game soldiers play in camp. Someone always wins; whoever carries these wins more often.

name: Lamp of Prometheus
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Lamp of Prometheus — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A clay lamp lit, the story goes, from the coal the Titan stole for mankind.
details: major · +2 mana at dawn and +1 commander Spell Power. · expanded content
lore: A clay lamp lit, the story goes, from the coal the Titan stole for mankind. It has never gone out.

name: Ogham Staves
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Ogham Staves — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Twenty letters cut as notches on yew staves, each a tree.
details: major · +15% spell damage. · expanded content
lore: Twenty letters cut as notches on yew staves, each a tree. Poets cast them to read fate and, when needed, to write it.

name: Omamori Charm
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Omamori Charm — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A silk pouch from a shrine, holding a prayer no one may read.
details: treasure · +1 Luck. · expanded content
lore: A silk pouch from a shrine, holding a prayer no one may read. Opening it would let the luck out.

name: Star Compass
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Star Compass — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A needle that points not north but toward the nearest place worth seeing.
details: minor · +2 hexes of adventure vision. Wayfarer’s Kit. · set: Wayfarer’s Kit · expanded content
lore: A needle that points not north but toward the nearest place worth seeing.

name: Stone of Fál
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Stone of Fál — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. The third treasure: a stone that roars when the rightful king steps upon it.
details: relic · +1 Luck and +1 commander Defense. Unique. · set: Treasures of the Tuatha Dé · expanded content
lore: The third treasure: a stone that roars when the rightful king steps upon it. A fragment of it hums under the hand of a true leader.

name: Sun-stone Codex
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Sun-stone Codex — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A folding book of bark paper that counts the days of five suns.
details: major · +10% spell damage and +1 commander Spell Power. · expanded content
lore: A folding book of bark paper that counts the days of five suns. Its reader knows which hour belongs to which god.

name: Valkyrie’s Horn
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Valkyrie’s Horn — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. The choosers of the slain drink from it before they ride.
details: major · +1 morale and +10% battle experience. · set: Arms of the Einherjar · expanded content
lore: The choosers of the slain drink from it before they ride. Warriors who hear it blown know they are being watched — and judged.

name: Barding of the Hippeis
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Barding of the Hippeis — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. Bronze chest-plate for the horse of a cavalry noble.
details: minor · +1 commander Defense and +5% daily land movement. · expanded content
lore: Bronze chest-plate for the horse of a cavalry noble. Expensive, heavy, and much admired at festivals.

name: Horseshoe of Sleipnir
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Horseshoe of Sleipnir — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. A shoe thrown by the eight-legged horse as it leapt the gate of the dead.
details: relic · +20% daily land movement. Unique. · expanded content
lore: A shoe thrown by the eight-legged horse as it leapt the gate of the dead. Any mount that wears it forgets what tiredness was.

name: Saddle of the Wild Hunt
shown_on: Hero screen (paper doll, backpack); Artifact merchant; Battle result loot; Encounter reward preview; Encyclopedia
brief: Saddle of the Wild Hunt — draw the object alone, three-quarter view. On storm nights the Hunt rides across the sky.
details: major · +10% daily land movement and +1 commander Attack. · expanded content

name: The Silent Shore
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The storm has passed, but the Outer Lighthouse is dark. Open the tidal bridge, raise and train a trusted guard, and relight the first beacon.

name: Wings over the Pass
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The second beacon stands beyond the raiders. Free the Griffins’ nesting ground, choose Athena or Ares, and raise Windcrest Griffins to light the pass.

name: The Storm Beacon
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: Melas holds the great beacon’s lens on the storm plateau. Choose a crossing, activate both relays to unseal the ward gate, defeat Melas and light the last beacon.

name: Barrow Light
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: Spring is two months late and Kaldvik’s barrow has cracked open. Raise and bind a watch from the barrow, clear the frozen ford and cut the headland rune again.

name: The White Pack
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: A pack of white wolves cuts the south road to Birkaby, and it runs where the Grey Jarl tells it. Raise wolves of your own, cross the Varg-river, hunt the pack down and cut the wood’s rune.

name: The Valkyrie’s Price
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: Frost trolls hold the Valkyries’ aerie in the high fells. Break the ice-pass, free the aerie, win the trolls’ oath by gold or by force, choose Thor or Tyr and carry Battle Valkyries to the third rune.

name: Ice on the Sound
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: Only the Norns know the Grey Jarl’s oath. Raise Lindworms, take the ice-landing, light both way-cairns through the fog and read the water of the Norns’ Well — while a draugr crew walks the ice.

name: The Jarl of Hvitstrand
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: Jarl Ulfhild swore to keep the Grey Jarl’s winter for a frozen sea that keeps her rivals’ ships in harbour. Cross the Hvita, win a second god, take Hvitstrand from a living rival and break her oath.

name: The Giants’ Refuge
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The Grey Jarl froze the giants of Hrimgard into the glacier to guard his road. Climb the glacier wall, break the ice-wardens, win the Jotnar’s oath and defeat Hrafn the Hollow at the Glacier Gate.

name: Oathbreaker’s Hall
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The Grey Jarl waits in his hall on the oath-mound. Climb the plateau, cut both stones to open the barrow-gate, defeat the Jarl, decide the sword’s fate and seal the oath.

name: The Ember Dawn
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: For nine mornings the sun has risen red and low and gone down again within the hour. Raise a temple guard in Abedju, clear the canal lock and sing the morning hymn at the Obelisk of the East.

name: The Black Boar
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: A herd of black boars, fed and driven by the Hollow Lector’s men, roots up the west-bank fields of Nekheb. Raise jackals of your own, cross the river, hunt the herd down and reopen the Shrine of the Western Gate.

name: The Sculptor’s Price
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: In the quarries above Edfu the tomb-servants have stopped working. Break the hired guard on the cliff road, free the sphinxes’ terrace, win the ushabti covenant — by the sculptor’s price or by force — and take a god for the long night ahead.

name: The Drowned Library
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The House of Records at Per-Djehuty lies beyond the flooded marsh, behind a veil of grey mist. Raise river beasts, take the landing, light both pylon-fires to burn away the mist and read what the records say about the sun.

name: The Red Vizier
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: Paser, a vizier who crowned himself in the dusk, holds Per-Wadjet and the stela of the throne. Cross the river, take a second god, besiege his town and break the stela that names him king.

name: The Phoenix Rookery
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The bennu birds, whose rising is the sun’s own, are caged in their rookery under the cliffs of Iunu. Break the jailers, accept the bennu covenant, raise firebirds of your own and defeat Hekaib at the rookery gate.

name: The Twelfth Hour
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The barque of the sun is held in the Hall of the Coil, at the bottom of the night. Cross into the hours, open the gate with both horizon-stones, defeat Djedkhonsu and decide what becomes of the coiled dark.

name: The Unlit Lantern
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: On the night of the festival of the dead, not one lantern in Kagaribi would light. Raise a fox retinue, clear the bamboo bridge and relight the great stone lantern on the pass.

name: The Boar Lord
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: A giant boar and its herd run the rice terraces of Mizuhara and keep the spirits from the river lantern. Raise kappa of your own, cross the river, hunt the Boar Lord and relight the lantern of the mountain road.

name: The Crow Monastery
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The bell of the Crow Monastery on Kumoyama has stopped. Break the ronin on the mountain road, free the oni of the red hall from their clay jailers, win the tengu covenant — by the abbot’s price or by force — and take a kami for the road ahead.

name: The Spirit Sea
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The Hall of Mirrors stands on an island in the Spirit Sea, behind a fog that eats boats. Raise spider-women of your own, take the landing, ring both shrine bells to clear the fog and look into the mirrors for the Lantern-Eater’s home.

name: The Iron Daimyo
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: Lord Kurogane fences the wandering dead into his army and holds the Iron Castle and the Lantern of Oaths. Cross the river, take a second kami, besiege his castle and break the lantern that binds the dead to him.

name: The Kirin Meadow
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The kirin, whose coming marks a just age, are penned in their high meadow by the Lantern-Eater’s jailers. Break the jailers, accept the kirin covenant, raise kirin of your own and defeat General Oboro at the meadow gate.

name: The Last Torii
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The Lantern-Eater’s palace stands across the last stretch of the spirits’ road, behind the last torii. Cross the hills, light the sun stone and the moon stone, defeat Yamikage and decide what becomes of the road between the worlds.

name: The Cold Hearth
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: Beltane came and no fire would catch. Raise a war-band of pooka in Dún Caill, clear the ford of the alders and light the Beltane fire on the old stone.

name: The Iron-Bristled Boar
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: A boar with bristles like iron nails leads a herd through the fields of Dún Bera and keeps the folk from the ogham stone at the ford. Raise hounds of your own, cross the river, hunt the boar and cut the summer ogham again.

name: The Water-Horse Bargain
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The kelpies of Loch Eala have stopped coming to shore. Break the reavers on the hill road, free the banshees’ hill from the cairn-men, win the kelpie covenant — by the keeper’s bargain or by force — and take a god for the dark road ahead.

name: The Hall Beneath the Waves
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The hall of the sea-folk lies beyond the islands, behind a mist that came with the raiders. Raise selkies of your own, take the landing, light both headland fires to burn away the mist and ask the sea-folk where the Withered King keeps the broken branch.

name: The High Seat
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: Fiachra took the high seat at the ford in the long winter and holds it with the Withered King’s help. Cross the river, take a second god, besiege his fort and overturn the inauguration stone that names him king.

name: The Stags’ Wood
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The great horned stags of the deep wood are bound in iron by the Withered King’s jailers. Break the jailers, accept the stags’ covenant, raise stag spirits of your own and defeat Tadhg the Grey at the wood’s gate.

name: The Door of the Mound
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The Withered King holds the broken silver branch in his hall inside the great mound. Cross the barrow-hills, use the summer stone and the winter stone to open the door, defeat Dubhghall and decide what becomes of the silver branch.

name: The Cold Altar
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: On the night the years are bound, the new fire was never lit — someone put out the old one first. Raise a war-band of feathered serpents in Xochitla, clear the canoe ford and kindle the fire on the hill altar.

name: The Black Jaguars
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: A pack of black jaguar spirits, loosed by the Night-Knife, hunts the cacao groves of Tepeyolo and guards the altar of the morning star. Raise jaguars of your own, cross the river, hunt the pack down and relight the altar.

name: The House of Eagles
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The eagle warriors of Ocelotepec have stopped flying. Break the cultists on the mountain road, free the crocodiles’ cenote from the stone jailers, win the eagle covenant — by the elders’ price or by force — and take a god for the dark road ahead.

name: The House of Bats
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The House of Bats stands on an island in the great lake, behind a smoke that came with the raiders’ canoes. Raise camazotz of your own, take the landing, light both lake altars to clear the smoke and ask the bats where the Night-Knife keeps the stolen fire.

name: The Lord of Itzcalli
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: Tecuani, lord of Itzcalli, swore to the Night-Knife for the throne of the next age, and holds the road east. Cross the river, take a second god, besiege his city and break the stela of his oath.

name: The Fire Mountain
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The fire serpents, whose coils carry flame across the sky, are chained in the crater of the fire mountain. Break the jailers, accept the serpents’ covenant, raise fire serpents of your own and defeat Mazatl at the crater gate.

name: The Smoking Gate
shown_on: Campaign setup; Briefing; Debrief
brief: The Night-Knife keeps the old fire in his obsidian palace inside the smoking mountain. Cross the ash-hills, light the morning-star stone and the evening-star stone to open the gate, defeat Itztli and decide what fire the next years are bound with.

name: The Three Beacons
shown_on: Campaign setup
brief: A storm has extinguished the three signal beacons protecting the coast of Asterion. Lead Alexios through three short linked missions to reconnect the coast before its settlements abandon one another.

name: The Winter Oath
shown_on: Campaign setup
brief: The winter did not end. Kaldvik’s barrow has opened, white wolves cut the roads and the Grey Jarl wants back the sword the seeress Hervor took from his mound. Lead Hervor through seven linked missions to bind the long winter — and decide what becomes of the oath.

name: The Twelfth Hour
shown_on: Campaign setup
brief: The sun has stopped below the horizon. Lead the lector priestess Seshet through seven linked missions — from the red dawns of Abedju down through the hours of the night — to free the barque of the sun from the Hollow Lector and the coiled dark.

name: The Lantern Road
shown_on: Campaign setup
brief: The lanterns that guide the dead home have gone dark. Lead the shrine diviner Akane through seven linked missions — from the unlit festival of Kagaribi to the last torii — to relight the spirits’ road and face the Lantern-Eater.

name: The Silver Branch
shown_on: Campaign setup
brief: The silver branch that opens the mounds has been broken, and the year has stuck in its dark half. Lead the druid Orla through seven linked missions — from the cold Beltane of Dún Caill to the door of the great mound — to turn the year and face the Withered King.

name: The New Fire
shown_on: Campaign setup
brief: The fire that binds the years was put out before it could be renewed, and the sun is fading. Lead the day-keeper Itzel through seven linked missions — from the cold altar of Xochitla to the smoking gate — to bind the years again and face the Night-Knife.
